items: Section 1

A reverse-engineered, evidence-backed model of FinanceOS: what it does, why each part exists, how the client, server, database, jobs and external services fit together, what the business rules and calculations actually are, and what remains unknown. Every non-trivial claim carries a confidence chip and a file reference. Code is the source of truth; the 164 plan documents are cited only as intent.
FinanceOS in one paragraph

FinanceOS is a self-hosted, multi-user personal-finance system for the Indian market (₹, Apr–Mar financial year, UPI, NSE/BSE, AMFI mutual funds). It keeps one ledger of every money movement across bank accounts, credit cards, broker accounts and cash, fed by three ingestion paths: hand entry, Gmail alert emails read by an LLM, and PDF or Excel statement uploads parsed by a heuristic engine. On top of that ledger it computes credit-card rewards under user-defined rules, tracks investment positions and returns with FIFO lots and XIRR, amortizes loans and tracks peer lendings, lets the user build ad hoc reports and dashboards over sixteen datasources, opens on an editable Home dashboard next to an Inbox of what needs attention and an Upcoming list of what falls due, and answers natural-language questions through an LLM that writes SQL against tenant-scoped read-only views. It is a Spring Boot 3.3 / Java 21 / Oracle backend on one OCI virtual machine and a Next.js 16 / React 19 client on Vercel, joined by a session cookie relayed across origins. Confirmed
What problem it solves, and for whom

The evidence points to a single primary user who is also the developer: V2 seeds one admin user, signups are gated by a single shared invite code, and the operations runbook is written for one VM and one operator. Strongly inferred The product thesis, reconstructed from the transaction review workflow, is that ingestion is noisy and provisional : every automatically created transaction starts as "needs review" and is trusted only after a human, or a rule a human verified, confirms it. Statements are the reconciliation source of truth for Gmail alerts. Almost every derived figure (balance, position, reward, schedule) is recomputed from source facts on read rather than stored, a philosophy the plan documents name "recompute over incremental". Confirmed in code ; the rationale appears only in plans and javadocs.
What makes it more than an expense tracker
Three ingestion paths with dedup and a reconciliation model
A credit-card reward engine that models real issuer mechanics (exclusive and additive rules, marginal tiers, shared cap buckets, milestones, anniversary windows)
Broker-statement reconciliation that separates intraday square-offs from delivery holdings using the broker's tax P&L
Corporate actions that rewrite FIFO lots (split, bonus, demerger, merger, cash in lieu)
A self-service report builder and an LLM chat over read-only, tenant-filtered views

review Approve or fix categories in the review queue, merge duplicates, link transfers and refunds, verify rules

FinanceOS in 5 minutes (for a new developer)

Two repos, one folder. financeos-server (Spring Boot, port 6969, Oracle via Flyway) and financeos-client (Next.js, port 6970, proxies /api/v1/* to the server). Both have their own git history since 2025-12-31.

Everything is per user. A request's user id sits in a ThreadLocal; an aspect enables a Hibernate filter so every entity read is scoped. If a service method is not @Transactional the filter is off. Six native-SQL sites bind user_id by hand. Chat has its own DB-level tenancy.

The ledger is transactions . Unsigned amount plus type. Source tells you where it came from. review_type and a reason set tell you whether a human has trusted it. Categories are many-to-many. Links (transfer, refund, card payment) never mutate rows.

Derived numbers are computed on read. Balance = statement anchor plus later transactions. Position = FIFO replay of trades and corporate actions. Reward = rule engine over the ledger. Loan schedule = annuity walk over terms and events. None of these are stored, so there is no cache to invalidate but every read pays the full cost.
Slow work runs as jobs. Uploads, Gmail sync, price refresh, rule apply, import commits go through a DB-backed queue with two worker threads in the same JVM. The UI polls.

LLMs are a utility, not the product. A failover client tries Gemini, Groq and OpenRouter in a user-configurable order for categorization, email extraction and chat. Chat writes SQL against 14 allow-listed v_chat_* views as a read-only Oracle user.

The client renders twice. A Server Component fetches and seeds a TanStack Query cache; a client component hydrates it and does all later reads and writes. Filters live in component state; refresh loses them.

Apparent product philosophy
Provisional until confirmed. Ingested data is flagged, not trusted. Confirmed
Model reality, not a simplification. Cardholders vs plastics, marginal tiers, shared caps, intraday vs delivery, demerger cost carve-outs, cash in lieu. Confirmed
Recompute over incremental. Named in the loans and rewards plans and visible in every derived figure. Strongly inferred
Free-tier everything. LLM failover across free keys, a 1 GB VM with swap, Grafana Cloud Free. Strongly inferred from config comments and the runbook.
Defense in depth where it matters. Chat tenancy inside Oracle plus a SQL allow-list; account deletion verified against the data dictionary; ReDoS-safe regex rules. Confirmed
The reason a given workflow exists is recorded in plans/ and in unusually dense "why" comments, but not in any single product document. Where neither exists, this handbook says so.

FinanceOS is two independent git repositories that live side by side in one folder: financeos-server (Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.3.4 / Oracle, 688 main-source files, ~53k lines, 95 Flyway migrations, 132 test classes) and financeos-client (Next.js 16 App Router / React 19 / TypeScript, ~536 source files, ~85k lines incl. tests, 62 unit-test files, 70 Playwright specs). Section 5
Executive summary

Twenty-odd concepts explain most of FinanceOS. Each is derived from an entity or a computed structure in the code, not assumed. The single most important mismatch between product and implementation is that the product concepts users think of as stored values (balance, position, reward earned, EMI schedule) are computed on read ; the stored facts are transactions, trades, terms and rules. Module
Executive summary

Accounts model "where money lives": bank accounts, credit cards, broker (demat) accounts and a generic bucket for cash and wallets. Only bank and credit card accounts can ingest: brokers are fed by broker imports and generic accounts are manual, so neither carries an ingestFromDate watermark in its DTOs, neither shows a Statements action on its tile, and V88 cleared any stale watermark rows. Everything else hangs off them: every transaction carries a mandatory account_id , statements attach to an account, Gmail alerts are matched to an account by last-4 or by user-declared identifier aliases, and reward rules scope to a cardholder under an account. A second sub-model, Cardholder → Card , records who holds a card (primary or add-on person) and which plastic they carry, so that reissuing a lost card or adding a spouse's card does not corrupt history or reward scoping. Confirmed

Balances are computed, never stored : the latest non-rejected statement's closing balance acts as an "anchor" and only later transactions are added on top; without an anchor the balance is opening balance plus the signed sum of all transactions. Broker "balance" is portfolio market value plus cash. Closure is a single closed_on date that blocks card mutations but not new transactions or imports. Confirmed domain/account/BalanceMath.java:29-82

Each account has its own page at /accounts/[id] (tiles open it; the pencil on a tile edits), and the stored asset/liability and net-asset flags now feed the net_worth report datasource behind the Home "Net worth" KPI. Confirmed

Inputs: the anchor (latest statement by period_end DESC, created_at DESC with a non-rejected verdict, a period end and a closing balance; any account type), totalSum = Σ(CREDIT +amount, DEBIT −amount) over all transactions, postAnchorSum = same sum for transactions strictly after the anchor date, and the bank opening balance. Account type Anchor? Formula Notes
credit_card yes base = closing > 0 ? −closing : abs(closing) ; balance = base + postAnchorSum "You owe ₹X" becomes a negative cash position; the abs branch is a no-op guard for ≤0 values
bank_account yes balance = closing + postAnchorSum ; gap = (opening + totalSum) − balance , shown if |gap| ≥ 0.01 Gap badge flags ledger vs statement drift BankAccountTile.tsx:44-51
broker, generic yes balance = closing + postAnchorSum No opening-balance gap check
bank_account no balance = (opening ?? 0) + totalSum Pure ledger

State, invariants, idempotency

Account status is derived: closed_on null → ACTIVE; future → CLOSING; past or today → CLOSED. Computed in Java ( Account.getStatus , never called externally), in TypeScript ( getAccountStatus ), and once in a dropped DB column (V81). Three implementations of one trichotomy, one unreachable.

Module
Executive summary

The transactions table is FinanceOS's central ledger: every money movement, whether typed by hand, parsed from a Gmail alert, parsed from a statement, or uploaded from a file, becomes one row. Around it sit a many-to-many category taxonomy, an LLM-assisted "auto-tag, then a human confirms" categorization system with saved rules, a review queue that records why a row still needs a look, a read-only relationship graph for transfers, refunds and card payments, a duplicate-merge tool, and bulk card re-attribution. Confirmed

The implicit product thesis, confirmed by the code: ingestion is noisy and provisional; every ingested transaction starts as "needs review" and becomes trusted only when a person, or a rule a person verified, confirms it. Almost every other module (rewards, reports, chat, balances, loans) reads this table, so its invariants (one account per row, unique source message per user, well-formed review state) matter far beyond this package.

Statement path and reconciliation

StatementReconciliationService.reconcile : pick the best attachment (prefer an encrypted PDF) → fetch bytes → if encrypted, try every account's stored statement password until one opens it (this provisionally identifies the account) → StatementParseEngine → confirm account via the resolver on the statement's account number → StatementPersistenceService.createIfNew (SHA-256 of bytes, unique per account) → watermark-filter lines → match each line via TransactionMatcher.findBestMatch → promote matches to AUTO_REVIEWED; materialize misses as gmail_statement NEEDS_REVIEW rows keyed messageId:lineIndex . gmail/reconcile/StatementReconciliationService.java:90-320
Match step Rule
1 Card If the line has a card last4, candidates on a different known card are excluded
2 Amount Exact compareTo == 0
3 Direction Same TransactionType
4 Date |Δdays| ≤ gmail.ingest.date-window-days (default 3)
Ranking same-card first, then smaller date difference, then higher Jaccard token similarity of descriptions
Assignment Greedy 1:1 in parser line order; no global optimum

Executive summary

A user drops a bank or credit-card statement (PDF or Excel) into Transactions → Import ( /transactions/import ) and the system detects the transaction table, reads every line, derives each amount's sign by reconciling against the printed running balance, cross-checks totals against the statement's summary box, and imports the lines as transactions while deduplicating at the statement level (same file or period) and flagging suspected duplicate transactions. The parser is one generic heuristic engine , not a library of per-bank parsers; it is a line-by-line Java port of a Python reference script and Python is never invoked at runtime. Two materially different reconciliation paths share the same parser: direct upload only flags duplicates and never skips creating a row; a statement arriving as a Gmail attachment matches and promotes existing unreconciled alert transactions and creates new rows only for unmatched lines. Confirmed

Parser pipeline
detect Magic bytes only: %PDF , PK\x03\x04 (XLSX), OLE2 (XLS); no extension check server-side
words PDFBox text positions grouped into lines (3.8 pt tolerance); POI cells become words at synthetic x = col×100 with numerics rendered %,.2f ; repeated per-page furniture dropped

rows A line is a candidate if it starts with a date token, an amount exists within 7 lines, and it is not a summary line. Date format inferred by majority vote over 28 formats; a second format accepted if it parses ≥2 leftovers

build Per row: description before the date, drop value dates and ref/cheque column values, drop currency glyphs, treat adjacent +/− and Cr/Dr as sign flags, amounts need a decimal point or comma grouping; continuation lines attached by proximity; yearless dates get the period's year

sign Balance oracle : cluster amount columns by x (12 px); score each column as a running balance by the fraction of rows where |Δbalance| equals another amount on the row (±0.011); best score ≥ 0.6 wins → mode balance-chain ; sign = direction of Δ. Fallback: header keywords (debit/withdrawal vs credit/deposit), else the busiest column with default sign −1 for credit cards, +1 otherwise, then an opening/closing reconciliation retry (±0.51) SignAssigner
summary SummaryFieldHarvester regex-labels about 19 fields (total due, minimum due, due date, credit limit, previous balance, purchases, reward points…); Cr flips dues-type signs
verdict See decision table
# Condition Verdict
1 checksum ok AND chainValidationPct > 95 AUTO-INGEST
2 checksum ok AND mode starts with "opening/closing" AUTO-INGEST
3 checksum unknown AND (cross-total found OR card check passes) AUTO-INGEST
4 chainValidationPct > 50 OR cross-total OR card check NEEDS REVIEW
5 otherwise REJECT

Checksum: |opening + credits − debits − closing| < 0.011 , with a credit-card retry swapping debits and credits (±0.51). closing falls back to the last row's derived balance, so a clean self-referential chain can reach AUTO-INGEST with no printed balances at all. Possible false confidence StatementParseEngine.java:354-369

Card checks (±0.51): purchases = Σdebits; payments + credits received = Σcredits; previous + finance charges + Σdebits − Σcredits = total due. cardOk = third check, or first and second together. Credit-card detection is text.contains("credit card") || text.contains("credit limit") over the whole document; a bank statement mentioning an overdraft "credit limit" flips the sign default. Bill payment notifications and the notification platform

The statement is the bill. A credit card's current bill is its latest non-rejected statement with card details; nothing else is stored. CardBillService computes the bill on read for the Bills due widget ( GET /api/v1/bills , optional ?accountId= to narrow to one card), the Inbox, Upcoming and the hourly notification tick, so they can never disagree.

Settlement precedence: a manual mark ( POST /api/v1/bills/{statementId}/mark-paid , paid_marked_on / paid_marked_amount on statement_credit_card_details , V90) wins; otherwise non-excluded credits dated after the period end count as paid when they are the card-side member of a CC_PAYMENT link or a member of a REFUND or REVERSAL link (refunds count as payment since 2026-10-08, a user decision); unlinked credits are only surfaced as "possible payments" (at most 5) for the user to confirm and never close a bill.

Status: NO_DUE (total ≤ 0), DUE_UNKNOWN (parser found no due date or total; fixed with PATCH …/details ), OPEN , PARTIAL , PAID , OVERDUE (due date passed, not paid in full), and AWAITING_STATEMENT (2026-10-08). Closed cards and bank statements never carry a bill. The list sorts OVERDUE, DUE_UNKNOWN, OPEN/PARTIAL, AWAITING_STATEMENT, NO_DUE, PAID, then by due date and card name.

Awaiting rows: listBills returns every open credit card. A card with no live statement gets an AWAITING_STATEMENT row whose statementId , period, due date and totals are all null; only the account fields, unbilledAmount and nextStatementExpectedOn are filled. Awaiting rows are never notified and never become Inbox rows: the tick calls build directly and never sees them.

unbilledAmount : card spend not yet on a statement, the sum of non-excluded DEBITs dated after the live statement's period end (all non-excluded DEBITs for an awaiting card), never negative. Credits never reduce it, because payments and refunds count towards the open bill instead. Null when the statement has no period end. The client's BillCardState.unbilled JSDoc still says "net of refunds", which is out of date. TransactionRepository.sumIncludedDebitsAfter , sumIncludedDebits

nextStatementExpectedOn : the end of the BillingCycles cycle that contains the day after the latest non-rejected statement with both period dates. It can already be in the past when a statement is late (the widget shows the lateness), and is null when the card has no dated statement. Both extras are filled only on the read path ( buildEnriched ); the notification tick skips the extra queries.

Send log = two columns. last_notified_kind / last_notified_on hold the most advanced kind already sent (or deliberately skipped) in the fixed sequence RECEIVED / DUE_MISSING → DUE_n (larger n first) → OVERDUE (repeats daily) → PAID . A kind is sent only when it ranks later than the marker, which makes the tick idempotent and gives catch-up after downtime for free: the most urgent reached kind goes out once with the real days-remaining text and the ones it overtook are never sent.

Producers: StatementCreatedEvent (after commit, StatementPersistenceService.createIfNew ) sends the statement digest immediately when the new statement is the card's current bill; BillNotificationScheduler runs BillNotificationService.evaluateUser hourly (IST, notifications.tick-cron ) for every user with push on and a registered device, gated by the user's send hour. Statements ingested more than 7 days after their own due date (45 days after period end without one) are history and never notify.

Delivery: Web Push only. core/push/WebPushCrypto implements RFC 8291 ( aes128gcm ) and RFC 8292 (VAPID, ES256) on JDK primitives — no push library — and is checked against the RFC's Appendix A vector. VAPID keys come from PUSH_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY / PUSH_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY ( GenerateVapidKeys ); unset means push is off and the tick only records markers. 404/410 from the push service prunes that device.

Preferences: one user_notification_settings row per user (master switch, send hour, reminder offsets CSV, per-kind JSON map, device subscriptions as a JSON array, at most 10) plus accounts.notifications_muted per card. Markers advance even when nothing can be sent, so enabling push later never replays a backlog.

Client: the Bills due widget ( components/bills/BillsDueWidget , 2026-10-08) replaced the hard-coded BillsDueCard on /dashboard . It is the bills_due built-in on the seeded Home dashboard and the Bills section of the account page. billCardState.ts maps each card to a phase: overdue (OVERDUE), arrived (OPEN, PARTIAL, DUE_UNKNOWN) or awaiting (AWAITING_STATEMENT, PAID, NO_DUE; shows unbilled spend and the expected statement date, flagged late once that date has passed). Rows sort overdue, then arrived by due date, then awaiting by expected statement date. Awaiting cards with no unbilled spend collapse into one "Nothing pending" group at the bottom. A header line totals To pay (arrived and overdue) and Unbilled. Actions work in place: mark paid in full or partially, undo, confirm a possible payment, set missing details. ?bill=<statementId> or ?card=<accountId> rings and scrolls to a row; /upcoming?bill=<statementId> does the same for its own bill row and hosts the shared Mark-paid dialog. BillStatementActions sits inside the statements dialog; /settings/notifications (this device, what to send, card mutes, devices); sw.ts push / notificationclick handlers over lib/pushPayload ; lib/push wraps PushManager . iOS delivers Web Push only to a Home Screen install.

The Inbox: in-app surface of the notification kinds

Since 2026-10-08 the Inbox ( /inbox , GET /api/v1/inbox ) is the in-app surface of all 13 NotificationKind switches. It is computed on read from the producers' own rows and marker columns by one InboxCollector per inbox kind, and it is strictly read-only: it never calls NotificationProducer.evaluate , never advances a marker and never runs the rewards engine, so opening it cannot cause a push. The per-kind push switches in /settings/notifications do not filter the Inbox. Muted cards and loans stay out of it. The full model (sections, snooze, dismiss, the Inbox widget) is on M11 . Module
Executive summary

A small DB-backed job queue ( jobs , job_artifacts ) runs every slow or external-dependent operation off the request thread: statement ingest, Gmail sync, price refresh, rule apply, investment import commit and broker reconcile commit. Requests return 202 {jobId} immediately and the UI polls. The history page is /settings/activity (heading "Activity"), and finished user-started jobs also appear as Inbox rows. The worker is a @Scheduled poller (every 2 s, plus an after-commit "poke") inside the same JVM with two threads; claiming is an atomic conditional UPDATE, cancellation is cooperative, and retry always creates a new job row. Confirmed domain/job/JobWorker.java , JobService.java
State machine

There is no INTERRUPTED status; it is an error code on FAILED. Retrying a STATEMENT_INGEST whose artifacts were purged throws "artifacts expired, please re-upload". succeed , fail and markCancelled do not guard on current status, so an out-of-order cancel racing a success could overwrite SUCCEEDED. Medium, latent

Module
Executive summary

The portfolio tracker for stocks, ETFs and mutual funds held in "broker" accounts. A user maintains an instrument catalog (symbol, exchange, ISIN, AMFI code, Yahoo ticker), records buy and sell trades with itemized charges, and sees positions (FIFO lots, average cost, current value, realized and unrealized P&L, XIRR), dividends, and SIP progress. A daily job at 19:00 IST refreshes prices from AMFI (mutual funds) and Yahoo Finance (stocks, ETFs). Corporate actions (split, bonus, demerger, merger with fractional cash-in-lieu) rewrite lots without re-entering trades. F&O is a standalone realized-only ledger. Broker exports are imported through two pipelines: a plain importer (used in practice only for mutual-fund CAS PDFs) and a reconciliation pipeline that uses the broker's tax-P&L statement to separate intraday square-offs from delivery holdings. Confirmed

Two facts shape everything: nothing about a position is stored (every read replays all trades and corporate actions through FIFO), and charges are excluded from cost basis (only XIRR is fee-aware), which contradicts the original plan document. Dependents: net worth via HoldingValuationService.getBrokerMarketValue , the report datasources positions / realized_lots / portfolio_value / fno_trades, the chat portfolio tool, and the investments pages.

Calculation: FIFO position engine

domain/investment/InvestmentService.calculateHoldingPosition:427-762 builds one date-sorted timeline per holding and walks it once. Same-day order: CA-seeded lots (0) → corporate actions (1) → transactions (2), so a CA applies to the lots that existed before that day's trades.

Day collapse : when a trade_settlement_classifications row exists for (broker, instrument, day), that day's raw rows collapse into at most one synthetic delivery buy and one delivery sell (residual after removing intraday quantity and value); the intraday net (sell value − buy value) goes straight to intradayRealized and to an XIRR flow of sell − buy − dayCharges .
Buy : push Lot(qty, costPerUnit = price, buyDate) . Cost excludes charges (comment at line 601: "Clean cost basis"). XIRR outflow = qty×price + charges.

Sell : consume oldest lots; per lot emit a RealizedLot (buy date, sell date, qty, values, P&L, holding days, term = days > 365 ? long : short). Realized = qty×sellPrice − matched cost (gross). XIRR inflow = qty×price − charges. If lots run out, log a warning and stop; the remainder is silently dropped from realized P&L.
Corporate action : split/bonus multiply qty by ratioTo/ratioFrom and divide cost per unit by it (openCost invariant); demerger multiplies parent cost per unit by 1 − pct/100 ; merger clears all lots.

Example ( RealizedLotsParityTest ): buy 10 @ ₹100, buy 20 @ ₹150, sell 15 @ ₹200 → first lot fully consumed (10 × 100 = ₹1,000), 5 from the second (5 × 50 = ₹250) → realized ₹1,250 ; open 15 @ ₹150, openCost ₹2,250. The holding's realized always equals Σ per-lot P&L because both come from the same loop (parity contract with the reports engine).

Invisible-fee example : buy 100 @ ₹500 delivery. Groww charges: brokerage min(0.1%, ₹20) = ₹20; STT 0.1% = ₹50; exchange 0.00297% ≈ ₹1.49; SEBI ₹0.05; stamp 0.015% = ₹7.50; GST 18% of (brokerage + exchange + SEBI + DP) ≈ ₹3.88; total ≈ ₹82.91 . The lot still costs ₹500.00/unit. Selling flat at ₹500 shows ₹0 realized while ₹82.91 was lost; only XIRR reflects it. Dividend receipt reconciliation

A dividends row is an expectation : Yahoo events times quantity held ( suggested ), a CAS line ( import ) or a hand-typed entry ( manual ). V89 adds the question "did the money actually arrive?", answered by linking the row to the bank credit it arrived as. The link is a direct nullable FK dividends.transaction_id (same pattern as lendings.transaction_id ); the dividend amount is never changed by linking, it stays the gross figure the XIRR and FY summaries use. Several dividend rows may share one credit (an interim and a special payout often land as a single credit). domain/investment/dividend/DividendReceiptService.java

Status is derived at read time, not stored. Only two states are stored, in receipt_status , as a manual note: received_untracked (it landed in a bank account FinanceOS does not track) and not_received (confirmed missing). The other four come from DividendReceiptWindows.derive in this order: linked → received ; manual note → that note; expected-payout window has not ended (end ≥ today) → awaiting ; window end ≤ the user's bank coverage ( MAX(transaction_date) over their bank_account transactions, from DividendReceiptStatusResolver ) → overdue ; otherwise unverifiable . "Unverifiable" exists because absence of a credit proves nothing when the statements stop before the window ends: the bank data has simply not reached that date, so the row is neither confirmed nor overdue. The chat dictionary uses the same wording ("not matched yet", never "missing").
Matching is suggestion only. GET /reconciliation proposes credits; the user confirms each (or "Confirm all"); nothing links automatically. Confirmed by code

Preview → commit contract : the server parses the file at preview and echoes every row; the client posts those rows back with skip and instrument choices; commit trusts client-echoed quantities, prices, dates and charges verbatim and re-checks only duplicates and instrument existence. Medium trust boundary
Dedup gate : matchByExternalRefOnly = (source == zerodha_tradebook) ; otherwise exact tuple (date, type, qty, price). No tolerance. No DB constraint; concurrent commits could double insert.

Instrument resolution : ISIN → local symbol + alias → catalog search (ISIN first) → auto-create shell; likelyDelisted (ISIN present, search exhausted) sets yahooSymbol = null so the instrument is manual-price-only and valued at cost. Preview and commit implement the chain separately.
Charges come from the file only (Zerodha and Groww exports have none; CAS attaches stamp duty within 3 days). Reconciliation attaches Zerodha delivery-sell charges from the tax-P&L rows.
Reconciliation algorithm (two sources)
dedup Executions (tradebook) deduped by the full tuple (tradeId, orderId, date, isin, type, qty, price, time); tradeId alone is not unique
classify Tax-P&L rows bucketed INTRADAY / STCG / LTCG / BUYBACK / FNO → intradayMap[isin][date] = {qty, buyValue, sellValue}
split Per (scrip, day), walk executions in order: intraQty = min(remaining target, e.qty), rest delivery; split rows get refs suffixed -I / -D
events Day-level delivery events by value subtraction: delivBuyQty = dayBuyQty − intradayQty, delivBuyVal = dayBuyVal − intraBuyVal
fifo Delivery-only FIFO per scrip; unmatched sells → DATA_GAP ; classifier delivery sells exceeding the tradebook → synthesized CA_EXIT_ sell at average price with OFF_MARKET_EXIT (buybacks, tenders)
commit Writes investment_transactions (source import, charges verbatim), trade_settlement_classifications (insert-if-absent only, never updates), fno_trades ; fires a price refresh per instrument

Example ( IntradayClassificationTest.partialIntraday_straddlingBuy_isSplit ): buy 15 @ ₹100 and sell 10 @ ₹110 same day with classifier intraday 10 → the buy splits into 10 intraday + 5 delivery; holdings show 5 @ ₹100; intraday P&L ₹100 stays out of cost basis. The Java matches scripts/reconcile_trades.py and adds per-execution tagging, off-market exits and snapshot validation. Without a tax-P&L file everything is treated as delivery. The per-row settlement_type is a display hint that "will lie on mixed straddle days" (V40 comment); recomputeClassificationForDay rebuilds the authoritative day row after every manual create, update or delete using min(intraday buys, intraday sells).

Module
Executive summary

Answers three questions for an Indian credit-card user: what did I actually earn (rewards report and per-transaction lines), what would this swipe earn (rule tester and simulator), and which of my cards should I use (the Card Picker). It is a single stateless, compute-on-read engine: nothing about "how much a transaction earned" is ever stored. Every report, lines page or recommendation re-runs the user's rule set over the ledger. Confirmed domain/reward/RewardCalculationService.java:47-55 (javadoc: "Pure compute-on-read rewards calculator. No persisted reward state").

Why it exists: Indian issuer cards have idiosyncratic rate, cap, tier and milestone shapes (Axis ACE shared caps, Amex slab points, HDFC Infinia tiers); the research doc in plans/credit-card-reward-calculation-research.md catalogues 16 issuers and the engine primitives were derived from it. Strongly inferred from plan docs; the code itself does not state the rationale.
Level 1 · Product view
Who uses it
A cardholder with one or more credit cards who wants to know real earned value and to pick the best card per purchase.
What they configure
Reward rules (match conditions + accrual), cap buckets shared across rules, milestones, and per-account settings (anniversary date, default reward type, point value in ₹).
What they get

Per-account report (cash ₹ and points both shown; points valued at the card's point value count toward the ₹ gross), per-transaction lines with a reason code, cap and milestone status, per-cardholder split, ranked card recommendations.

Product model vs implementation model. Users think "my card". Code has two things: Account (the card product or line, e.g. "HDFC Infinia") and Cardholder (the person swiping: primary or add-on). A physical plastic is a third thing, Card . Reward scoping keys off account + cardholder, never off the plastic, so a lost-card reissue never disturbs reward configuration. Confirmed V82 rewrote reward_rules.card_id to cardholder_id ( V82__credit_card_model_v2.sql:128-138 ).

Users also assume "one deal per transaction". In code a transaction can earn under several rules at once: one exclusive winner plus every matching additive bonus, each with its own cap. A transaction id is therefore not a unique key for a report row.
Level 2 · How it behaves
Rule matching decision table
All predicates are optional; unset means wildcard. All axes are ANDed; the category/MCC axis is an internal OR. RewardCalculationService.matches():555-615
# Axis Rule is rejected when… Null / empty behaviour
1 Cardholder scope rule has a cardholder and the transaction's cardholder differs, or cannot be resolved on a 2+-cardholder account unset → any cardholder
2 Category OR MCC rule lists categories and/or MCCs and the transaction hits neither both unset → skipped
3 Merchant pattern neither description nor sourced description matches (CONTAINS / STARTS_WITH / EXACT / REGEX, case-insensitive) unset → wildcard
4 Channel channel list non-empty and transaction channel null or not listed empty → wildcard
5 Day of week day list non-empty and day not listed empty → wildcard
6–7 Amount band amount < minAmount or amount > maxAmount null → no bound
8 EMI treatment EXCLUDE_EMI and isEmi, or ONLY_EMI and not isEmi INCLUDE → wildcard
9 International EXCLUDE_INTL and isIntl, or ONLY_INTL and not isIntl INCLUDE → wildcard
Fee treatment is not a predicate. EXCLUDE_FEE nets the labelled convenience fee out of the basis after a match: basis = max(amount − convenienceFee, 0). RewardCalculationService.basisFor():527-532
Precedence: exclusive chain, additive stack
There is no single total order across all rules. resolveTxnFacts() partitions matching rules by stacking : RewardCalculationService.java:449-525

EXCLUSIVE rules in descending priority (ties by created_at ascending) form a first-match chain. A 0% exclusive rule that matches wins and blocks everything below it (this is how "no rewards on rent" is modelled). If the winner's cap is exhausted: FALL_THROUGH (default) tries the next exclusive rule; STOP emits a zero line and ends the chain.
ADDITIVE rules each accrue, clamp against their own cap, and always emit a line, stacking on the exclusive result. Priority among additive rules is cosmetic.

Worked example from RewardRecommendationServiceTest.exclusiveFallThrough_plusAdditiveStacking : 5% exclusive with a ₹0 cap (exhausted) falls through to a 1% exclusive base (₹10 on ₹1,000), plus a 0.5% additive bonus (₹5) → ₹15 across two lines. The reorder endpoint reassigns priority = N…1 from the UI order, so drag order is the exclusive-chain order. RewardRuleService.reorder():139-164

L3 Caps and cap buckets: clamp formula and boundary behaviour

Owner is the shared bucket id when cap_bucket_id is set (bucket cap and window replace the rule's own), else the rule id. A shared bucket is drained jointly by every rule pointing at it. capOwner():779-781 , effectiveCap():731-741

Counter scope : ACCOUNT (one counter) or PER_CARDHOLDER. An unattributed transaction charges the primary cardholder's counter for counting, but for matching a cardholder-scoped rule it only resolves when exactly one cardholder exists. This asymmetry is deliberate per code comments. counterCardholderId():1164-1175 , matchCardholderId():1154-1162

Example: 2% rule, ₹50/month cap per cardholder. Unattributed ₹2,000 → ₹40 (primary counter 40/50). Primary's own ₹1,000 (raw ₹20) → ₹10 PARTIAL_CAP. Add-on's ₹2,000 → ₹40 on a separate counter. RewardCardScopingTest.perCardholderCap_unattributedSpend…

Window expansion : before fetching, the requested range is widened to cover every whole cap/tier/milestone window intersecting it, so a mid-month filter still sees earlier cap consumption; only lines inside the original range are summed. evaluate():298-346
L3 Milestones

Basis SPEND (₹) or TXN_COUNT (with an optional per-transaction floor min_txn_amount , "Amex style"). Eligibility is an independent include/exclude category/MCC list (exclude wins; empty include = everything not excluded). milestoneStatus():1075-1124

Payout types: CASH_VALUE (counted in totals) or INFO_TRACKER (progress only, e.g. fee-waiver target; never scored). Payout timing WINDOW_END or ON_ACHIEVEMENT ; a milestone is counted in the summary only when its payout date falls inside the requested range, which prevents double counting across adjacent reports.

ONE_TIME windows require both active dates (service-validated only; no DB CHECK). Recurring windows are walked with a 500-iteration guard that throws "Date range too large" rather than looping. evaluateMilestones():1038-1073

The recommender scores unreached milestones with a fractional proximity credit = (delta / threshold) × payout: ₹12,000 toward a ₹1,00,000 / ₹1,000 milestone scores ₹120. The report never does this. RewardRecommendationService.java:180-237

Invariant Enforced Tested Gap

Module
Executive summary

Three kinds of "money owed on a schedule": formal loans (home, car, personal, education, gold, two-wheeler, consumer durable, other) with a computed EMI amortization schedule, rate revisions, prepayments, foreclosure, itemized charges and bank-transaction matching; person-to-person lendings as a plain two-way ledger per counterparty (no interest, no schedule); and an obligations list (the Upcoming page, list and calendar views) merging upcoming and overdue EMIs and lending due dates with credit-card bills and expected statements. The plan doc explains the split: banks compute interest on a schedule, informal debts do not. Intent doc plans/loans-module-plan.md:13

The schedule is never stored; every read recomputes it from the loan's terms and events. Payments record only (installment seq, date, amount, transaction id); the interest/principal split shown everywhere is the schedule's theoretical split. Outstanding principal follows the schedule, not payments. Outside this module, loans and lendings are read by the notification producers, the Inbox EMI and lending collectors, ObligationsService and the net_worth report datasource (active loans' outstanding principal as liabilities, counterparties' net positions as assets or liabilities); see M11 · Home, Inbox & Upcoming . Lending ledger entries and loan payments/events/charges reference a bank transactions row via a direct nullable FK on the referencing table ( ON DELETE SET NULL ) — never through transaction_links . Export ledger as text

The person page ( /loans/lendings/[counterpartyId] ) renders the ledger as plain text for sharing — the Web Share API ( navigator.share ) when the device has it, the clipboard otherwise. Pure client code: lib/lendingExport.ts builds the text from the entries the page already loaded (the first 200); the dialog in [counterpartyId]/components/ExportLedgerDialog.tsx only wires selection, names and toggles into it. Nothing touches the server.
Rule Behaviour

Selection Every loaded entry by default. Chips: All ; Since last settled — the entries after the most recent running-balance zero (if the ledger is square right now, the cycle just settled; hidden when it would equal All); None . Running balances are float sums, so "zero" is |b| < 0.005 .

Wording Two optional name fields. A party is its name when given, otherwise a pronoun: Adarsh lent Rahul , I lent Rahul , Adarsh lent you , I lent you ; balances read Rahul owes Adarsh ₹… / you owe me ₹… . The app's first-person labels ("You repaid", "They repaid") never appear — the reader is the other side of the ledger.

Opening balance Optional, statement-style. Defaults to the running balance just before the first selected entry (zero when it is the first) and follows the selection until edited; Reset restores the derived value. Present → an Opening balance: line, running balances continue from it, and the last line is Closing balance: = opening ± selected entries. Cleared → no opening line and the last line is Net of listed entries: .

Content toggles Notes (on); expected-return dates (off, principal entries only); totals (on — the four gross lines, zero lines omitted, hidden for a single entry); running balance after each entry (off).
Never printed Entry counts, the linked bank transaction (account, date), the person's private notes, any footer.

Remembered per device "Your name" and the toggles — localStorage key financeos.lendingExport.v1 , every access in try/catch. "Their name" always prefills from the person; selection and opening balance never persist.

Actions Footer is always primary + Close (the dialog primitive allows two actions and hides its X when a secondary exists): primary is Share when navigator.share exists, Copy otherwise; on share-capable devices Copy sits beside the preview instead. A dismissed share sheet ( AbortError ) is silent; any other share failure falls back to Copy. Share/Copy are disabled with nothing selected, Close never is.

The same change made the person page's and the loan page's actions viewport-complete: one renderActionBar(isMobile) is rendered in a desktop Card ( hidden lg:block ) and inside PageActionBar (whose slot is lg:hidden ) — the convention every browser page already used. Until then the two detail pages exposed Settle up / Edit / Delete only below 1024px.

Invariants, concurrency, contradictions

Σ principal = principal (structural). One payment per seq (service + DB unique). One loan/lending reference per transaction was DB-unique across all four tables through V85; V86 keeps loan_events / loan_payments / loan_charges.transaction_id globally unique in the DB but drops the DB constraint on lendings.transaction_id — split bills (several lending rows, same transaction, same implied direction) are now a service-only rule in TransactionReferenceValidator.validateForLending , not schema-enforced; loan-vs-lending exclusivity is still service-only on both sides, as before. Deleting an event rejects if any payment's seq exceeds the new schedule length, but not if the seq now means a different installment. Foreclosure amount is unreconciled. Close has no zero-balance guard.

No @Version ; TOCTOU windows on payment seq and transaction linking fall through to raw DB constraint errors. Re-posting addPayment without a seq settles the next installment (not idempotent); the UI always passes a seq. Batch re-post is rejected wholesale.

400-vs-404 lesson (hit and reverted while building the linking feature, 2026-09-07): LendingService.getLendingAndVerifyOwnership briefly switched from findById ( EntityManager.find , which bypasses the Hibernate userFilter that Lending has always carried) to the fetch-joined JPQL findWithRefsById — but that query is @Filter -scoped, so a foreign row is invisible and 404s before the ownership check runs, breaking the established "foreign row → 400 Security Breach" contract the rest of the module relies on (an existing E2E assertion caught it). Reverted to findById ; the linked transaction now loads lazily inside the transaction instead. Generalizes: on any @Filter entity, the single-row ownership-check path must use findById , never a filtered fetch-join — list paths ( findAllWithRefs , findByCounterpartyIdWithRefs ) still use fetch-joins to avoid lazy N+1, since those don't gate on ownership of one specific id.

SET NULL orphaning is observable, not blocked : deleting a transaction referenced by a loan/lending row is allowed (decision: a duplicate bank row is a legitimate delete) and silently nulls the reference; TransactionService logs OBLIGATION_REF_ORPHANED per orphaned ref on both single and batch delete so the event is at least visible server-side — the delete confirmation UI only warns using the obligationRefs already on the row being deleted, there is no server-side block.

Split sum is not enforced : several lendings rows may point at one transaction (V86) with no check that their amounts sum to, or stay under, the transaction's own amount — see Lending ↔ transaction linking .

Contradictions : ±₹20 tolerance vs plan exact match; client running balance vs server net (same sign convention; same-day order non-deterministic because the API sorts only by entry date); FY boundary configurable on the server ( financeos.reports.fiscal-year-start-month ) but hardcoded to April in useLoanQueries.ts:63-69 and LoanAmortizationSchedule.tsx:27-33 ; loan.types.ts hand-written while lending.types.ts re-exports generated types; browser "Monthly EMI" sums the current page only; rate_type has no behaviour; the EMI matcher does not exclude transaction_links members the way the newer lending matcher does (see the decision table above).

Dead or suspicious : LoanRepository.findByStatus(LoanStatus) unpaged overload unreferenced; LendingRepository.existsByCounterparty_Id leftover from pre-V48; duplicate aliases loansApi.addPayment/createPayment , delete/remove ; summary aggregation lives in the controller.

Module
Executive summary

A self-service BI builder: the user picks one of sixteen datasources (transactions, investment trades, dividends, F&O trades, positions, realized lots, portfolio value, loan payments, loan tax summary, lendings, reward earnings, reward milestones, reward caps, net worth, upcoming obligations, needs attention), builds a KPI, Chart or Table definition (filters, group-bys, measures, sort, granularity including Indian financial year), previews it, and saves it as a Report row with a JSON definition. A Dashboard is a named 100-column grid of widgets; a widget is either a saved report (reportId, layout) or a built-in from a fixed server catalog (builtinKey, params, layout). The dashboard computes nothing itself. Confirmed

Two facts matter most. First, the landing page (Home, /dashboard ) is the default dashboard, seeded once per user with built-in widgets : a net-worth KPI over the computed net_worth datasource, the Inbox, Bills due, Upcoming and a "Spend this month" report (see M11 · Built-in widgets and Home seeding ). The old "financial summary" endpoint is still a hardcoded stub that returns zeros and is never called. Second, grouping or filtering transactions by category uses a fan-out join with no de-duplication, so multi-category transactions can be double counted; the sibling chat views already solved this with LISTAGG . Execution pipeline

Saved reports are re-parsed and re-validated on every run (a field removed from the catalog fails loudly; there is no migration for stale definitions). domain/report/ReportDataService.java:58-93 Ad hoc runs and built-in dashboard templates share ReportDataService.runDefinition(type, datasource, definition, page, size) : validate and run for the current user, nothing persisted.
Transactions datasource semantics

Amount is signed CREDIT positive, DEBIT negative. The spend measure is the same money spend-positive: CASE WHEN t.type = 'DEBIT' THEN t.amount ELSE -t.amount END (debits positive, refunds and income negative), so a spend chart needs no sign flip; it was added instead of changing the sign of amount . "Total spend" is SUM(spend) or SUM(amount) filtered to DEBIT.

Link type and card joins (fixed 2026-09-30). linkType is a joined column ( lk.link_type from a per-transaction MIN over its links) because Oracle rejects a scalar subquery in GROUP BY (ORA-22818); grouping by it used to 500. The cards join is aliased cd : it and the categories join both used c , so card, cardholder or relationship combined with category could never run.

No default exclusions. isExcluded , isTransferLeg , isRefundLeg , isUnderMonitoring and reviewType are opt-in filters. The builder seeds isExcluded is false on a new transactions report as a UI convenience only; it is not re-applied on edit or on ad hoc runs from elsewhere.
isTransferLeg and isRefundLeg are correlated EXISTS subqueries (no fan-out).
The source and channel filter values come from TransactionSource and TransactionChannel (fixed 2026-10-04: source listed the dead "gmail"/"manual", channel was missing ATM). See Transactions .

Category double counting. Critical JOIN_CATEGORIES is a fan-out LEFT JOIN added whenever category is a dimension, column, sort key or filter . A purpose-built EXISTS-based SqlPredicates.category() exists in the same package with the comment "so the join never fans out an aggregate" but is never called by the report engine (only by the transactions list). ChartReportExecutor.countRows uses COUNT(DISTINCT id) to fix the row count but not the SUM. domain/report/engine/TransactionQueryBuilder.java:90-92 , SqlPredicates.java:46-69
Usage Grouped by category? Effect Severity
Chart or pivot grouped by category, SUM(amount) yes Each category gets the full amount; the cross-group total exceeds real spend Medium ambiguity, undocumented
KPI or chart filtered by category in (...) , grouped by something else or not at all no A transaction matching two of the filtered categories is summed twice into one bucket Critical untested
Raw table selecting category n/a Duplicate rows, each with the full amount High

Filter values : GET /report/datasource/{name}/values ( ReportFieldValuesService ) returns, for every dynamic enum field, the distinct values that occur in the user's data, exactly as filters compare them: SQL datasources run SELECT DISTINCT <expr> per field under the user-scope predicate; computed datasources collect from rows() (multi-valued fields flattened). Capped at 500 per field, case-insensitive sort. It also returns options (value, label): for a field with an idField (reward datasources: card, rule, milestone, cap) the value is a stable id, so a saved filter survives renames and relabels (e.g. a same-named rule on another card, or end-date & clone); a filter that holds a label still matches. The client ( useReportDynamicOptions ) fetches it only once a filter uses a dynamic field, refetches on remount and window focus, and shows an error hint if the request fails.

Filter fields (2026-10-04): a FieldDef carries an optional filterable flag, serialized only when false (absent = filterable). notFilterable() sets it; canFilter() reads it and is deliberately not a bean getter, so the JSON has no extra property. The validator rejects a filter on such a field, and the builder's filter editor leaves it out ( filterableFields in components/reports/catalog.ts ); it still works as a grouping and a column. Grouping-only today: every Billing cycle dimension ( cycleGrouping() ; filter on Date with the billing-cycle operators instead), reward_earnings.rewardYear and txnCount , lendings.counterpartyId and transactionId , and loanId on both loan datasources. Static enum values are derived from the Java enums, never hand-written. transactions.cardholder ( NVL(ch.person_name, 'Unattributed') ) and loan_tax_summary.financialYear are dynamic enums, so they get a dropdown of real values instead of free text. reward_earnings.earned is labelled "Earned (₹ or points)" because it sums cash and points together. Saved reports were not migrated (none existed); a saved filter on a grouping-only field now fails validation.

In-memory semantics (2026-09-30) : charts group null dimension/series values as (none) like the SQL path and the pivot; enum is_not / not_in keep rows with no value on both paths (SQL adds OR expr IS NULL ); a List value is multi-valued (filters match any element, negated ones require none, grouping fans out, raw tables join with commas); pie and donut ignore a series split, as on the SQL path; achieved (milestones) and capHit / cycleFallback (caps) are Yes/No dimensions usable as columns and groupings.

Dashboards

dashboards.widgets is a JSON array in one CLOB (not a child table). DashboardWidget record: id, kind ( report | builtin ; null, as in widgets stored before built-ins, means report), reportId, title, layout {x, y, w, h} on a 100-column grid, builtinKey, params. Validator: x ≥ 0, w ≥ 1, x + w ≤ 100, y ≥ 0, h ≥ 1; no upper bound on y or h and no overlap check (intentional); a report widget needs a reportId; a built-in needs a registered builtinKey, valid params and w ≥ the entry's minW (50 or 100); an unknown kind is a 400. The response adds a builtin ref (key, label, minW, kind, templateType, href) for built-ins, null when the key is no longer registered; built-in widgets never touch the report repository.

Built-ins ( BuiltinWidgetRegistry ): net_worth (KPI template), attention (labelled Inbox, component), upcoming (table template, days param, default 14) and bills_due (component). Template data comes from POST /dashboards/builtins/{key}/data , which runs the template through runDefinition with no report row; the catalog is GET /dashboards/builtins . A built-in can be added many times, resized down to its minW and removed, never edited; Open (only built-ins have it) drills to its href; the overflow menu offers Edit report (report widgets), Duplicate as my report (template built-ins) and View full page. On a phone the grid becomes a single-column stack. Full detail in M11 · Built-in widgets and Home seeding .

Home seeding : the first GET /dashboards or /dashboards/default per user claims users.home_seeded_at (V93) with a conditional UPDATE and creates the default "Home" dashboard; POST /dashboards/home/restore creates a fresh one on demand (201).
At most one default per user, enforced by the V15 partial unique index on CASE WHEN is_default = 1 THEN user_id END plus a clear-then-set in the service; a lost race maps to 409.

Landing render: dashboard/page.tsx lists dashboards (the list call seeds Home first; a 404 is treated as "none" and the empty state offers Restore Home), picks the default or the first, and prefetchWidgetData runs every report widget, every template built-in (through the built-in data endpoint) and, when an Inbox widget is present, the Inbox list in parallel on the server under the exact TanStack keys the widgets' queries use, so first paint needs no refetch. src/lib/dashboards.server.ts
Save sends the entire widget array via PUT; no per-widget PATCH. Only the "set default" star has an updatedAt conflict guard; editor and builder saves are last-write-wins.

Dead : GET /api/v1/dashboard/summary (returns zeros, status "skeleton", no service; E2E asserts the stub as a product gap), DashboardService.toSummary() and DashboardSummaryResponse , client keys.dashboards.summary() . The dashboards spec said the summary "stays as-is" until an accounts/positions datasource exists; the net_worth datasource and built-in now cover that need, and the stub was not removed. Executive summary

FinanceOS calls third-party LLMs (Google Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter) for two background tasks, transaction categorization and Gmail email extraction, and for one interactive feature, "Chat with your data". Because no provider is paid for centrally, the LLM layer is built around failover across free tiers : FailoverLlmClient walks an ordered list of (provider, model, key) "buckets", skipping any in cooldown, so a single free key or the user's own bring-your-own keys keep the app working across daily quota resets. Strongly inferred from config comments ("widest free-tier headroom").

Chat is a bounded tool-calling loop (6 iterations, 180 s soft, 270 s hard, 290 s transport) in which the model writes read-only SQL executed as a separate Oracle user CHAT_RO that can see only tenant-filtered v_chat_* views. The model never sees raw data except what a capped query returns. Transcripts are held only in React state and are lost on refresh. Confirmed
Failover algorithm
Step Rule
1 Task → group data-chat → CHAT; categorize , email-extract , anything else → DEFAULT ( LlmTasks.groupOf )
2 Chain order user's saved LlmTaskPref rows for the group → else llm.default-routing.<group> → else legacy llm.tasks.<task>.chain → else LLM_CHAIN
3 Expand option models list → one entry per model; pinned model → one entry; else the provider's full model list
4 Keys user's ACTIVE keys for the provider by position; env key only if allowNoKey (none today; reserved for a future self-hosted provider)
5 Fan-out Gemini with no pinned model: model-major (model A across every key, then model B), so one key earns a separate daily quota per model; otherwise one bucket per key
6 Dedup by keyId:model , first-seen order
7 No buckets LlmException(NO_KEYS) without an HTTP call
8 Walk skip buckets in cooldown; call up to attemptsPerProvider (2)
success reset counters, update last_used_at , return
401 / 403 mark the key INVALID in the DB (one-way), advance
429 BucketStateRegistry.handle429 sets cooldown, advance, no same-bucket retry
FATAL / BAD_OUTPUT count a failure, advance
RETRYABLE (5xx, IO) retry same bucket with 1000 ms × 2^(n−1) capped 8000 ms, honouring Retry-After
exhausted LlmException(FATAL, "chain") with concatenated reasons (≤1500 chars) and the soonest cooldown expiry

Cooldowns ( BucketStateRegistry , in-memory, per keyId:model ): a 429 whose body contains "PerDay", "per_day" or "quotaId" + "Day" → cooldown until midnight America/Los_Angeles (Gemini's reset), applied to any provider; otherwise max(Retry-After, 60 s). Independently, three consecutive failures within 60 s open a 60 s circuit. State is lost on restart. The "per-day 429 truncation" fix: classification reads the 4000-char response body, not the 200-char log preview (tested by test429BodyWithQuotaIdBeyond200CharsSetsMidnightPtCooldown ). llm.retry.cooldown-ms is configured but never read; 60000 is hardcoded. Keys and routing preferences

llm_api_keys (V72, V76): provider, key_ciphertext AES-256-GCM under LLM_KEYS_MASTER_KEY (must decode to 32 bytes; unset disables BYOK with an ERROR at boot), key_last4 , label, position, status ACTIVE|INVALID, last_used_at ; unique (user, provider, position) with a two-phase reorder (offset 1000, flush, renumber). The provider CHECK was dropped in V76; validity is app-only. Create validates the raw key against the provider first (Gemini x-goog-api-key , OpenRouter /key , others /models ). There is no master-key rotation tool; rotating it breaks every stored key.

llm_task_prefs (V76, V77): task_group CHAT|DEFAULT, position, option_id (V77 replaced provider+model columns). The menu is five fixed options (gemini-chain, gemini-flash-chain, groq, openrouter-free, openrouter-glm), reorder only; chat does not inherit the default group's order. V78 deleted Cerebras rows.

Shipped default: chat leads with the Flash chain (fast first token for a wall-clock-bound loop); background leads with the full Gemini chain. Gemini model order comes from llm.providers.gemini.models ; model-catalog is display metadata only and must be updated in parallel.
Chat orchestration

UI Composer → useChatStream.executeSend builds the transcript (clarify turns serialized as "[You asked the user to clarify]: …", last 10 messages, ≤2000 chars each) → fetch('/api/chat') app/(protected)/chat/lib/useChatStream.ts:71

proxy app/api/chat/route.ts relays the session cookie to POST /api/v1/chat/stream and pipes the SSE body back ( maxDuration 300 ); maps 503 CHAT_DISABLED and 429 CHAT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED / CHAT_BUSY to typed JSON

controller ChatController.streamChat : feature flag ( chat.enabled and CHAT_RO credentials) → daily quota 30 per user (in-memory, IST date via AppTime ) → semaphore 2 concurrent → worker on a 4-thread pool with UserContext copied across → 15 s heartbeat; a failed heartbeat cancels the worker

prompt 22 hard rules (tenant reminder, never fabricate, results are untrusted data, decline non-finance, clarify at most once, prefer SQL aggregation, use calc for math, Oracle dialect, no UUIDs in answers, block rules, report-draft rules 17–21, clarify round-trip rule 22) + dictionary.md (loaded once at construction, needs a restart to change) + grounding block (today, active FY, accounts and up to 60 categories with UUIDs, cached 5 min per user) + transcript + this turn's step results

loop Each iteration the model must choose run_sql | call_tool | calc | clarify | final_answer . Tool enum is every registered ChatTool (adding a component makes it callable). Budget: 6 iterations; forceFinalAtMs = min(180 s, max(30 s, emitter − 90 s)) = 180 s forces the final-only schema; hardDeadlineMs = max(10 s, emitter − 20 s) = 270 s returns without another call; SSE emitter closes at 290 s. Same failure signature twice → "do NOT retry" instruction; three times → forced final.

sql ChatSqlExecutor : ChatSqlValidator → wrap in FETCH FIRST 201 ROWS ONLY → ChatDbSession (3-connection CHAT_RO pool, ALTER SESSION SET CURRENT_SCHEMA , DBMS_SESSION.SET_IDENTIFIER(userId) with a bound parameter, fail closed if no user) → 5 s statement timeout → JSON ≤16,000 chars with truncation flags → CLEAR_IDENTIFIER on close; SQL errors genericized

answer final_answer Markdown plus optional blocks JSON, re-validated by ChatBlocksParser (≤4 stats, ≤2 charts of ≤50 categories × ≤6 series, ≤2 tables of ≤8 columns × ≤50 rows, ≤3 follow-ups, one report draft with UUID-shaped id and ≤8000-char definition); invalid blocks are dropped, not fatal

Check Rejects
Raw text @ (dblinks), /*+ hints, DBMS_* , UTL_* , SYS.
Statements more than one; anything but a JSQLParser Select ; SELECT INTO

Executive summary

Three read surfaces that sit on top of the other modules (server 9e02b6c, 9be54db, 1ef1d56; client 7dace73, d92c84f, fbf53be). Home is the user's default dashboard, seeded once per user with four built-in widgets and one saved report. Inbox is a grouped action list (Act now, Needs a look, Info) computed on every read from the same rows the push producers read, with per-row snooze, dismiss and undo. Upcoming is the obligations list: EMIs, lending returns, card bills and expected statements over a 1–12 month horizon, shown as a list or a calendar. None of them stores rows of its own. The schema adds only users.home_seeded_at (V93), inbox_item_state (V94) and the reward alert notified_on dates (V95). Confirmed

Three facts matter most. First, listing the Inbox is strictly read-only : no collector calls NotificationProducer.evaluate , advances a notification marker or recomputes an engine, so opening the Inbox can never send a push or change what the next tick does. Second, Upcoming and the net_worth datasource isolate every section in its own read-only REQUIRES_NEW transaction ( SectionRunner ), so one broken section returns no rows instead of a 500; the Inbox has no such isolation. Third, push deep links point at the Inbox only when the Inbox lists the item ; otherwise they open the bill on Upcoming or the installment on the loan page. Confirmed

InboxService.list runs in one read-only transaction: it loads the user's inbox_item_state rows, asks every InboxCollector bean for its rows ( collect(userId, today) , today = AppTime.today() ), drops rows whose state hides them today, and sorts by section (act_now, needs_look, info), then severity (critical, warning, info), then date (undated last), then title. GET /inbox/summary costs the same as a list and returns only the counts. domain/inbox/InboxService.java

A row is an InboxItemResponse : key , kind , rowType ( item = one thing to act on, summary = a count behind one link), severity , section , title, subtitle, href , amount, date, count (summary rows), actions and refs (statement, account, loan, counterparty, connection or job id). An action is {type, label, href, payload} ; navigation actions carry an href , mutation actions a payload with exactly the ids they need. summary is {actNow, needsLook, info, badge} with badge = actNow + needsLook .

State: snooze, dismiss, undo
Call Rule Failure

POST /inbox/{key}/snooze {until} Upsert snoozed_until for (user, key). Hidden while today < until; the row returns on until . Item rows only 400 when until is not after today; 400 "can be dismissed but not snoozed" for the two summary keys
POST /inbox/{key}/dismiss Sets dismissed_at once; hidden for as long as the state row exists. Allowed on any key —
DELETE /inbox/{key}/state Undo: deletes the state row, clearing both snooze and dismissal; a key with no state is a no-op —

all three Key must be non-blank, at most 200 characters, no whitespace or control characters. Keys are not checked against current rows (the E2E sweep allowlist records this as by design). Each call returns the fresh InboxResponse 400 for a malformed key

Keys are per subject and, where it matters, per period: a bill is per statement, an EMI per installment, a reward row per window, so a new period produces a new row even after the previous one was dismissed. The client removes the row optimistically, shows a toast with Undo (which calls the DELETE), and restores the cached list on error ( components/inbox/useInboxActions.ts ). Snooze presets are Tomorrow, In 3 days and Next week, plus a date picker. The UI shows snooze and dismiss only where the row's actions offer them; bill actions open the shared bill dialogs, every other action is a link.

Push deep links. The push producers now link to /inbox?item=<key> only when the Inbox would list the item at that moment: bills when OVERDUE, DUE_UNKNOWN, or OPEN/PARTIAL due within 7 days (else /upcoming?bill=<statementId> ); EMIs when due within 7 days or overdue (else /loans/<id>?installment=<seq> ); lending returns, expected statements, Gmail reconnect and Gmail attention always. Job pushes go to /transactions/import (statement ingest) or /settings/activity?type= . The Inbox page resolves ?item= once against the first loaded list: it scrolls to the row or shows "That item is already handled". See M4 · Bill payment notifications for the producers themselves.
The attention report datasource is the Inbox rolled up per kind (see M9 · Computed datasources ). Dividend suggestions are deliberately not an Inbox kind: they stay a live scan on the dividends page.

The calendar view ( CalendarGrid ) replaced the old /loans/calendar page. Card bills can be marked paid in place ( MarkPaidHost ), and ?bill= scrolls to and rings that bill.
Bills due card states

CardBillService.listBills now returns a row for every open credit card. A card without a live statement is an AWAITING_STATEMENT row (a new BillStatus , never notified): statement id, period, due date and totals are null, and only the account fields, unbilledAmount and nextStatementExpectedOn are set. GET /bills accepts an optional accountId filter (the account page uses it). The notification tick still calls build directly, so it never sees the awaiting rows and never pays for the two extra queries.

unbilledAmount : SUM of non-excluded DEBITs on the card dated after the live statement's period end (all of them for a card without a statement), floored at 0. Credits never reduce it, because payments and refunds count towards the open bill instead. Null when the statement has no period end.
nextStatementExpectedOn : the end of the BillingCycles cycle after the latest non-rejected statement with both period dates. It may already be in the past when the next statement is late.

Refunds pay the bill : a credit after the period end that is linked as REFUND or REVERSAL now counts towards paidAmount exactly like a CC_PAYMENT link (user decision). Unlinked credits are still only "possible payments".

The client maps each BillStatus to a phase ( components/bills/billCardState.ts ): OVERDUE → overdue ; OPEN, PARTIAL, DUE_UNKNOWN → arrived ; PAID, NO_DUE, AWAITING_STATEMENT → awaiting . Rows sort by phase (overdue, arrived, awaiting), then by due date (arrived and overdue) or expected statement date (awaiting), then by card name. An awaiting card with no positive unbilled spend goes into the collapsible "Nothing pending · N cards" group, whose quiet line reads "Paid on d" for a marked bill, else "Statement expected d" or "Statement due since d" when late. The header totals are the sum of what is left to pay on arrived and overdue cards and the sum of positive unbilled spend. Actions stay in the widget: confirm a possible payment, Mark paid, Undo (manual marks only), Set details (DUE_UNKNOWN). BillsDueWidget replaces the hard-coded BillsDueCard that used to sit on /dashboard ; it highlights ?bill=<statementId> or ?card=<accountId> and opens the Nothing pending group when the highlighted card is inside it.
Section isolation (SectionRunner)

Upcoming and the net_worth datasource are composite reads: several independent sections (four obligation kinds; accounts, loans, lendings). Each section was meant to degrade to "no rows" when it fails. A plain try/catch around the section was not enough: when the failing collaborator is a @Transactional bean that joined the caller's transaction (a service or a Spring Data repository), its interceptor has already marked that shared transaction rollback-only, and the caller's commit then throws UnexpectedRollbackException , so the whole read returned 500 despite the catch. The Spring/H2 integration tests in 9be54db found this.

The section's own @Transactional collaborators enable the tenant filter on entry, on the new session. ObligationsSectionIsolationIntegrationTest makes the card-bill section throw and asserts EMI and lending rows still come back through the service proxy and over HTTP; NetWorthSectionIsolationIntegrationTest does the same for the loans and lendings sections through ReportDataService and the built-in widget endpoint. Confirmed

The Inbox is not isolated. Medium InboxService.list calls every collector inside one read-only transaction with no per-collector catch, so one collector that throws fails GET /inbox , the summary badge, the Inbox widget and the attention datasource together. domain/inbox/InboxService.java

Section 6
Executive summary

One Oracle schema (Autonomous DB in production, a local Oracle container in dev and E2E), migrated exclusively by 95 Flyway scripts; Hibernate ddl-auto is none , so Flyway, not the entities, is authoritative. It grew from a single-user MVP (V1 seeds one admin user in V2) into roughly 57 tables plus 16 read-only chat views covering the ledger, a three-layer credit-card model, Gmail and statement ingestion ledgers, a rebuilt investment stack, loans and lendings, a large reward-rule configuration, a job queue, LLM keys, reports and dashboards, notification markers, and the per-row Inbox state. Confirmed

Three schema-wide facts: primary keys are VARCHAR2(36) UUID strings (transactions and jobs self-assign UUIDv7); money is NUMBER(19,4) almost everywhere with two scale-2 exceptions; and every Instant -mapped column is now TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE , which took three fix passes (V27, V46, V71) after ORA-18716 outages. No table has @Version or a soft-delete column; deletion is real and relies on FK cascades.

Tenancy at the database level

34 of 50 entities carry @Filter(name="userFilter", condition="user_id = :userId") , enabled by HibernateFilterAspect on every @Transactional method. Join tables and JobArtifact inherit through parents; GmailBackfillDemand is keyed by user id; GmailSyncCursor has a user_id and no filter .

Native SQL exists through EntityManager.createNativeQuery in six classes ( AccountRepositoryCustomImpl , TransactionRepositoryCustomImpl , TransactionReferenceValidator , ChartReportExecutor , KpiReportExecutor , TableReportExecutor ); each binds user_id explicitly or receives pre-filtered ids. The database analyst's grep for nativeQuery annotations found none; the createNativeQuery sites were confirmed separately. Confirmed
Chat uses Oracle-side enforcement ( CHAT_RO + session identifier + view predicates), independent of the JVM filter.
No FK asserts that a transaction's account and card, or a rule's account and cardholder, belong to the same user or account; single-column FKs only.

Navigation-redesign queries (server 9e02b6c). InboxItemState carries the filter, and its repository methods ( findByUserId , findByUserIdAndItemKey ) also bind the user explicitly. The review and Gmail counts behind the Inbox summary rows ( countByUserIdAndReviewType , countByUserIdAndReviewTypeAndReason , countByUserIdAndStatusIn ) and the seeder's report lookup ( findFirstByUser_IdAndNameAndDatasourceOrderByCreatedAtAsc ) bind user_id explicitly. The card unbilled sums ( sumIncludedDebitsAfter , sumIncludedDebits ) are keyed by account id only. They are safe because CardBillService.listBills passes only the caller's own cards and the filter is active. The EMI and lending Inbox collectors call getAllLoansWithSchedule() and findAllWithRefs() with no user argument, so they rely on the filter alone. That holds because InboxService.list is @Transactional . markHomeSeeded is a bulk JPQL UPDATE on users (the root, no filter) keyed by the caller's id from UserContext . Confirmed

Per-section transactions keep the filter : SectionRunner (Upcoming and net_worth ) runs each section in its own REQUIRES_NEW read-only transaction. A new session starts without the filter. Each section's collaborators ( LoanService , LendingService , CardBillService , AccountService , Spring Data repositories) are @Transactional , so HibernateFilterAspect enables the filter again on the new session. A future section that queried through a non-transactional bean would run unfiltered. Strongly inferred from the aspect's pointcut.

V1-era tables ( accounts , transactions , categories , holdings , statements , dividends ) still have nullable user_id ; a NULL row is invisible to the filter, a silent orphan. Every table from V26 onward declares NOT NULL. Strongly inferred single-user origin.

Business meaning of the database
The ledger ( transactions and satellites): every money movement, however it arrived.
The wallets ( accounts , detail tables, cardholders , cards ): where money lives and who holds which plastic.
The sources (Gmail tables, statements): ingestion machinery and the bookkeeping that prevents double ingestion.
The derived layers (reward configuration, holdings as identity, classifications): insight computed on read rather than stored.
The configuration (category rules, reward rules, reports, dashboards, LLM prefs): how the user teaches the app.
The operations tables (jobs, sessions, LLM keys): infrastructure.

The attention layer (notification markers on producer rows, inbox_item_state , users.home_seeded_at ): what the app has already told the user and what the user chose to hide. The Inbox, Upcoming and Home figures themselves are computed on read and never stored.

Sections 12 and 63
Executive summary

Three ingestion paths feed one ledger; four derivation engines read it. Data is created at the edges (email, PDF, broker file, form), normalized once (LLM extraction, parser, import resolver), persisted as facts, and never aggregated into stored summaries. Enrichment happens in two places: LLM categorization at ingestion and corporate-action replay at read. Synchronization is one-directional from sources to the ledger; reconciliation exists only between Gmail alerts and statements. Confirmed
Flow 1: external source → ledger → derived views
Flow 2: user input → validation → derived data → UI
Where data is created, transformed, aggregated, cached, persisted, deleted, synchronized, enriched

Section 7
Executive summary

A Next.js 16 App Router application (React 19, TypeScript) that renders every authenticated screen twice on purpose: a Server Component page.tsx makes the first API calls and seeds a per-request TanStack Query cache, then a client component hydrates that cache and owns all later reads and writes through browser fetch . The app began as pure Server Components plus Server Actions (the README still describes that design) and was migrated module by module onto TanStack Query in September 2026 while keeping the RSC first paint. Confirmed

Two API layers are both live: lib/apiClient.ts (server-only, 1,349 lines of per-domain wrappers) for RSC prefetch, and lib/api/client.ts (browser openapi-fetch) for interactivity. Three refresh mechanisms coexist. List filters live in component state, not URLs, except the Activity (job history) page; a few deep-link parameters ( ?item= on /inbox, ?bill= on /upcoming, ?account= on /transactions/import and /rewards/rules) only select or highlight a row. Chat transcripts live only in React state.
Architecture
Two paths to one API: browser components call same-origin /api/v1/* through the Next rewrite; Server Components call API_BASE_URL directly and hand the result to the browser as a hydrated cache.
Product information architecture

Desktop. Sidebar renders a Chat button in its header and the mounted NavTree below it: four top-level links (Home, Inbox, Upcoming, Accounts), five collapsible groups built from the *_MODULE constants in components/layout/navigation/navItems.tsx (a group starts open when the current path belongs to it), then Settings as one link. Highlighting uses isNavItemActive : exact match, or a prefix match only when no longer registered href also matches. Instruments has no nav entry; HoldingsView links to /investments/instruments . Confirmed

Inbox badge. NavTree and MobileNav both read useInboxSummary() ( GET /inbox/summary , polled every 60 s, staleTime 30 s). The badge is summary.badge = act-now rows + needs-a-look rows (info rows never count), rendered by formatBadge as a rose pill, capped at "99+", hidden at 0. Every GET /inbox also writes the summary key, so the badge and the Inbox page agree. The protected layout does not prefetch it; the badge appears after the first client fetch.

Mobile bar. MobileNav is a floating bar (hidden at lg and above, slid away while the on-screen keyboard is open). getMobileNavContext(pathname) picks its items: Home / Inbox / Upcoming / Transactions by default; inside a group ( /transactions , /rules , /investments , /loans , /rewards , or /dashboards , /reports , /chat for Insights) it shows that group's short labels plus a left "X" link back to /dashboard. The right end is always the menu button.

Menu sheet. The menu button opens MobileMenuSheet , a bottom-sheet Dialog : a Chat row ("Ask your data"), an Accounts row, the five groups as chip rows (a chip whose label equals its group name reads "All", so Transactions shows All · Review · Rules · Categories · Import), a divider, a Settings chip group (Profile & appearance /settings, Connections /settings/gmail, AI keys /settings/llm-keys, Notifications /settings/notifications, Activity /settings/activity, Debug /debug), then the signed-in email and Sign out. The Settings chips are a local SETTINGS_ITEMS list, kept out of NAV_ITEMS on purpose so they do not affect sidebar prefix highlighting; /settings is active only on itself. Any link closes the sheet. Confirmed

Redirects (server redirect() in the old page files): /settings/ingest → /transactions/import and /settings/jobs → /settings/activity , both keeping the query string; /loans/calendar → /upcoming (query dropped). The Gmail page keeps its /settings/gmail route because the OAuth redirect URI points at it; only its label changed to "Connections".

The mounted NavTree still shows a plain "Needs Review" label with no count. getNavigationTree(needsReviewCount, inboxCount) and AppShellNav.tsx remain dead (zero importers outside each other).
