What Home is. Home is an ordinary dashboard named "Home" and marked default, seeded once per user. The claim is a conditional UPDATE of users.home_seeded_at (V93), so two concurrent first requests seed once and a failed seed rolls the claim back. The trigger is lazy: the first GET /dashboards or /dashboards/default . The seeded layout on the 100-column grid is Net worth (x 0, w 50) and Inbox (x 50, w 50) on the first row, then Bills due (w 100), Upcoming (w 100, params.days 14) and the "Spend this month" report widget (w 100). That report is a CHART (bar, dimension category , measure spend SUM, filters date this_month , type is DEBIT , isExcluded false, isTransferLeg false); restore reuses an existing report with the same name and datasource instead of creating another. Restore always creates a new Home and makes it the default; an older Home stays as a second dashboard. See M9 · Dashboards .

Built-in widgets. A widget is kind: "report" (has reportId ) or kind: "builtin" ( builtinKey + optional params ). The server's BuiltinWidgetRegistry defines four: net_worth (template KPI, minW 50, Open → /accounts), attention (label "Inbox", component, minW 50, Open → /inbox), upcoming (template TABLE over obligations , minW 100, param days 1..90, Open → /upcoming) and bills_due (component, minW 100, optional accountId param, no Open). A template carries a datasource and report definition run directly by ReportDataService.runDefinition with no report row; a component is drawn by its own client component. The editor lets a built-in be added several times (the Add widget dialog's "Built-in" list, with a params step when needed), resized but never below its minW ( validateWidgets and the server's DashboardValidator both check), and removed. In edit mode a built-in gets the title override, the half/full width toggle (disabled when its minW is the whole grid) and Remove, but no edit-report link: there is no report behind it to edit. In view mode Open appears only on built-ins; the overflow menu offers "Edit report" (report widgets), "Duplicate as my report" (template built-ins: copies the template definition with the widget's params into a new saved report via POST /reports) and "View full page".

There is no Bills Due card hard-coded into the page any more; bills reach Home only through the bills_due widget, and the old BillsDueCard is deleted. On a phone the view is DashboardStack : widgets in reading order (layout y, then x), KPIs 140 px tall, charts and tables 320 px, component widgets sized to content. Edit mode keeps the grid. Snooze and dismiss. Both upsert one inbox_item_state row per (user, key) (V94, unique). Snooze needs a date after today (the client's date dialog enforces min tomorrow; the server returns 400 otherwise) and is refused on summary rows; the row returns on the until date. Dismiss sets dismissed_at and hides the row until the state is cleared; since a bill keeps one key across due-soon and overdue, a dismissed bill stays hidden after it turns overdue. Undo is DELETE /inbox/{key}/state , which forgets both. Keys contain ":"; openapi-fetch percent-encodes the raw key, so the client must not encode it again. Debug · /debug
The diagnostics and debug interface provides real-time LogQL correlation and client-side error inspection:

Who sees what : Administrators (every signed-in user while ADMIN_EMAILS is unset; only the listed emails once it is set) see the full reference lookup tool powered by Loki queries, including HTTP request details, root cause analysis with diagnostic hints, interactive timeline entries with expandable stack traces, and on-demand raw log export. Non-administrators see a developer notice ("Send this reference to the developer…") and a local ring buffer of errors without Loki querying capabilities.

Client ring buffer : errorLog keeps up to 20 newest errors in localStorage under financeos:diagnostics:errors tagged by ownerUserId . It resets on account change or session expiration. Deduplication logic merges consecutive errors with the same reference and error code occurring within 3 seconds rather than appending redundant rows. Users can copy formatted diagnostic reports, share via Web Share API / clipboard, and clear history.

Toast error contract : When an API error occurs, toastError and toastErrorResult record the event in the client ring buffer and show a Sonner error toast displaying Ref <ref> with action buttons: Copy ID (copies reference to clipboard) and Debug (navigates directly to /debug?ref=<encoded> ).

ErrorState and DiagnosticsProvider : Root error boundaries render ErrorState displaying the page request ID or error digest with Copy ID and Debug links. DiagnosticsProvider wraps the protected layout, injecting pageRequestId from incoming HTTP headers, user admin status, and Faro telemetry sessionId .

Section 15
Executive summary

One shared Spring Boot backend serves every user's financial data from the same Oracle tables, and the client (Vercel) and API (OCI VM) are different origins. This module therefore answers three load-bearing questions: who is asking (an opaque FINANCEOS_SESSION cookie resolved by Spring Session JDBC), which rows may they touch (a Hibernate @Filter switched on automatically by an AOP aspect for 36 entities), and how do two origins share one cookie (the Next.js server re-mints the API's cookie on its own origin). There are no roles: every user has identical authority over their own data and none over anyone else's. Confirmed

Quality is high for the tenancy and deletion designs (declarative filter, delete-then-verify in one transaction, a build-time schema test). Three real gaps stand out: the Google OAuth state is generated but never validated Critical ; two Gmail bookkeeping entities lack the tenancy filter Medium ; and maximumSessions(5) has no session-registry cleanup Medium .

Error contract

Uniform envelope { code, message, details?, timestamp, errorId?, requestId } from GlobalExceptionHandler . requestId (20-character trace identifier) is present on every error response — matching the X-Request-Id HTTP header — including 401/403 responses generated by LoggingAuthenticationEntryPoint and LoggingAccessDeniedHandler . errorId (8-character Crockford Base32) appears only on unhandled 500s, so its presence tells the client "unexpected failure", while the real exception stays in server logs. RequestContextFilter also maps the incoming X-Session-Id header to MDC sessionId for log correlation.

Admin role (email allowlist)

FinanceOS uses an email allowlist configured via ADMIN_EMAILS as the first authorization tier beyond multi-tenancy. When the list is unset or blank, every signed-in user is treated as an admin (open, zero-config for a single-tenant deployment — a user decision of 2026-09-07); once at least one email is listed, only those emails are admins. Identity is still required: an unauthenticated request is 401 before the guard runs. The authenticated user's admin status is evaluated by AdminService.isAdmin and exposed on UserResponse.admin (consumed by /auth/me ). Endpoints restricted to administrators are guarded by AdminGuard (which throws AccessDeniedException → 403 FORBIDDEN for non-admins). This administrative tier gates the only cross-tenant read operations in the system — diagnostics lookups across Loki server and client log streams — and logs a structured audit event ( event=diagnostics.lookup with adminUserId , refType , ref ) for every query.

Section 8
Executive summary

A single Spring Boot 3.3.4 process (Java 21) hosts the REST API, the job worker and three cron schedulers. Requests pass a servlet filter that stamps a request id, then Spring Security (origin validation, session restore, user-context resolution, authorization), then thin controllers that validate DTOs and delegate to @Transactional services, where an AOP aspect switches on the Hibernate tenancy filter before any repository call. Errors are mapped to one JSON envelope. Slow or external work is enqueued as a job. Confirmed

Deviations from the typical pattern

Asynchronous 202 responses. Statement upload, price refresh, rule apply, import commit and reconcile commit return {jobId} ; the real work runs later in JobWorker with UserContext set manually. domain/job/JobWorker.runJob
Server-sent events. ChatController.streamChat returns an SseEmitter (290 s timeout) fed from a 4-thread pool with a 15 s heartbeat; the Next route relays it.
Cron threads have no user. Price refresh runs with an empty context and refreshes all users' instruments deliberately; Gmail sync wraps each connection in callAs(userId) .

Ingestion bypasses TransactionService.createTransaction . Gmail and file ingestion save Transaction rows through the repository directly, so create-path validation (non-zero amount) does not apply to them.
Two tenancy mechanisms plus chat's third. Hibernate filter; explicit user_id binds in native SQL builders; Oracle SYS_CONTEXT for chat.
Google OAuth callback lands on the client , not this server, so the session cookie is minted on the client origin. Gmail-connect's callback lands on the server because the user is already logged in.
Full-history recompute on read for balances, positions, rewards and schedules, with in-memory pagination for reward lines and instruments.

Self-proxy idiom. CategorizationService and TransactionService inject a @Lazy reference to themselves so intra-class calls hit the transactional proxy (comments cite bugs F2/F3); AccountDeletionExecutor was split into a separate bean for the same reason.
Controller-layer aggregation. LoanController.getLoansSummary sums outstanding principal itself; RewardReportController slices lines in memory.

Per-section transactions in composite reads. ObligationsService.upcoming and NetWorthDatasource.rows run each section through SectionRunner , whose Spring implementation opens a REQUIRES_NEW read-only transaction per section. A plain try/catch was not enough: a failing @Transactional collaborator (a service or Spring Data repository) that had joined the caller's transaction marked it rollback-only, so the outer commit threw UnexpectedRollbackException and the whole read returned 500 despite the catch. The integration tests ObligationsSectionIsolationIntegrationTest and NetWorthSectionIsolationIntegrationTest found this; a failed section now logs OBLIGATIONS_SECTION_FAILED / REPORT_NET_WORTH_SECTION_FAILED and yields no rows. The tenancy filter is re-enabled on the section's own session by its @Transactional collaborators. core/tx/TransactionalSectionRunner.java Confirmed

Read-only Inbox computed on read. InboxService.list asks one InboxCollector per kind for rows, drops those hidden by the user's inbox_item_state , and sorts. Collectors read the notification producers' own rows and markers but never call NotificationProducer.evaluate , never advance a marker and never run the rewards engine, so opening the Inbox cannot send a push or change what the next tick does. The only writes are snooze, dismiss and undo on a row key; each returns the fresh inbox so the client needs no second request. Unlike the obligations read, collectors are not isolated per section: an exception in one collector fails the whole GET /inbox . domain/inbox/InboxService.java Confirmed

One-time seeding on a GET. GET /dashboards and GET /dashboards/default call HomeDashboardSeeder.seedIfNeeded before reading. The seeder claims users.home_seeded_at with a conditional UPDATE … WHERE home_seeded_at IS NULL (V93), so concurrent first requests seed once and a failed seed rolls the claim back. domain/dashboard/HomeDashboardSeeder.java
E2E profile backdoor. E2eControlController and ScriptedLlmClient exist only under @Profile("e2e") ; the systemd unit activates prod only. Confirmed

Executive summary

230 operations across 40 controllers under /api/v1 (the count of operations in financeos-server/api-spec.yaml ), plus 6 e2e-only control endpoints. Client callers fall into two families: Server Components and server actions use lib/apiClient.ts 's *Api objects; client components use lib/api/client.ts ( api.GET/POST… ) inside TanStack hooks. Executive summary

Eight external services touch FinanceOS: Google OAuth (sign-in), Gmail API (alerts and statements), three LLM providers (Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter) behind one failover client, Yahoo Finance (quotes, search, dividend events), AMFI (mutual fund NAVs), Grafana Cloud plus Slack for telemetry, and Grafana Loki as an active read dependency for administrative diagnostics queries. Every integration fails soft: an outage degrades a feature (no price, no categorization, parked email, unavailable diagnostics) rather than breaking core transaction operations. In the E2E profile every one of them is replaced by WireMock and the suite proves zero unmatched outbound calls. Confirmed
Outbound integrations and their triggers. The Gmail sync cron runs seven times a day; the price cron once; LLM calls happen on demand from ingestion and chat.

Section 14
Executive summary

All automation runs inside the single server JVM: four cron schedulers (Gmail ingest, price refresh, job retention, the hourly notification tick), a two-thread job worker polling a DB queue every 2 s, after-commit event listeners (price refresh after trades, Gmail reactivation after account or card changes, job-finished and statement-digest pushes), and the boot-time sweep that marks orphaned RUNNING jobs as failed. There is no external scheduler, no message broker, and no second instance, so nothing can double-run but nothing fails over either. Confirmed Job mechanics are detailed in M5 .

Notes

Timezones : crons run in Asia/Kolkata; "today" inside handlers uses LocalDate.now(zone) for price code and AppTime.today() (IST via app.zone ) for every other business "today"; the production JVM itself is UTC. Fixed 2026-10-03

Tenancy on worker threads : runJob sets UserContext from the job row; cron price refresh deliberately runs without a user and touches all users' instruments; GmailSyncJobHandler asserts the connection belongs to the job's user.
Cron-global jobs (user null) are invisible and uncancellable through the API.
Notifications : Web Push from the hourly tick and the two after-commit listeners above. Client toasts on job completion; chat completion may raise a browser notification when the tab is hidden.

Push links : a push opens /inbox?item=<key> only when the Inbox would list that item, so a tap never lands on an Inbox without the row; otherwise it opens the item's own page. Bills: the inbox row when OVERDUE , DUE_UNKNOWN , or OPEN / PARTIAL due within 7 days, else /upcoming?bill=<statementId> ( BillMessages.href ). EMIs: the inbox row when due within 7 days or overdue, else /loans/<id>?installment=<seq> ( EmiMessages.href ). Lending returns, expected statements, Gmail reconnect and the Gmail attention digest always link to their inbox row ( lending:<cp> , statement-expected:<acct>:<date> , gmail-reconnect:<id> , gmail-attention ); a digest where every email lacks an LLM key opens /settings/llm-keys . Job pushes open the starting page ( /transactions/import for statement ingest, /investments for imports, else /settings/activity?type= ); reward alerts open /rewards?account= ; the statement review digest opens /transactions/review?account= . Keys and the 7-day window live in InboxKinds . domain/inbox/InboxKinds.java
Recalculation jobs : none exist. Balances, positions, rewards and schedules are computed on read, so there is nothing to recalculate.
Cleanup : job retention only. Gmail cleanup is user-initiated from the account form.
What is not automated : Gmail token revocation detection, corporate-action ingestion, dividend detection (manual scan), SIP execution, reconciliation of derived figures.

Money is BigDecimal in Java and NUMBER(19,4) in Oracle with two scale-2 exceptions; quantities are 8 decimals; rates are stored as percents. Rounding happens at well-defined points inside each engine (HALF_UP unless a reward rule chooses FLOOR) and, for display, once in the client at 2 decimals. The exceptions worth knowing: XirrCalculator uses doubles; client card utilization and the reward rule tester use JavaScript numbers; SQL report aggregates pass through unrounded; the in-memory KPI path rounds differently from the SQL path. Executive summary

Automated ingestion is idempotent by design (unique keys on message id, file hash and source message id). Manual creates are not (no idempotency keys anywhere). Reads are pure with one exception: the first GET /dashboards or GET /dashboards/default for a user seeds the Home dashboard once, guarded by a conditional UPDATE on users.home_seeded_at . The Inbox read stays pure (it never evaluates a notification producer), and its only writes are the user's snooze, dismiss and undo, which are idempotent per item key. No entity in the codebase carries @Version , so every concurrent edit is last-write-wins and every check-then-act race falls through to a database constraint error rather than a clean 409 with a friendly message. The single job worker and single VM mean scheduled work never duplicates. Confirmed

FinanceOS has exactly one built-in reconciliation mechanism between two independent sources, Gmail alerts against statement lines, plus a few advisory signals (bank reconciliation gap badge, statement checksum verdict, broker realized cross-check, holdings snapshot DATA_GAP). There is no job that checks derived numbers against anything, no correction workflow beyond edit and merge, and no audit trail outside single-transaction mutations. Because derived figures are recomputed from source facts, the practical question "how would we know FinanceOS is wrong" reduces to "how would we know the facts are wrong or the formula is wrong". The workflows that explain most of the system, each with its sequence, the code involved and failure points. The nine critical paths at the end are the ones whose failure produces wrong financial information or blocks the product. Confirmed
Journey 1: Open the app and land on Home

A new user's first GET /dashboards (or /dashboards/default ) seeds Home through HomeDashboardSeeder.seedIfNeeded : the conditional UPDATE claims the seed so concurrent first requests seed once, and a failed seed rolls the claim back for the next request. Home holds Net worth, Inbox, Bills due, Upcoming (14 days) and the "Spend this month" chart; the page renders the default dashboard (or the first one) with a full-width switcher. On a phone the widgets stack in one column. /investments/dividends → a dividend row exists, created by Detect Dividends (Yahoo, source=suggested ), a CAS import ( import ) or the manual dialog ( manual ) → its receipt badge reads Awaiting while the expected-payout window (see M6 ) has not ended, and No bank data (status unverifiable ) once it has but the imported bank statements stop earlier → the user imports the bank statement (or Gmail sync lands the credit) → the badge becomes Overdue if the window is now inside bank coverage with no credit linked → Reconcile panel → Find matches → GET /investments/dividends/reconciliation returns, per dividend, scored candidate credits with reason chips ("Exact amount", "Net of 10% TDS", "Says dividend", "Names the company", "Split multiple? check expected amount") and a tier label (Exact / Net of TDS / Fuzzy) → the user picks a candidate and presses Confirm (or Confirm all ); when the credit is lower than gross by a plausible withholding gap, "Record TDS ₹x" is pre-ticked and can be unticked → POST /investments/dividends/reconciliation/confirm with {dividendId, transactionId, updateTds} per item → DividendReceiptService.confirmMatches validates each ( validateForDividend ), sets transaction_id , writes tds = gross − received only if opted in, TDS is null and the gap is 0–25 % of gross, and returns per-item results (one failure does not abort the rest) → the row shows Received with "+₹ · account · date" and a variance hint if the credit differs from the expected net by more than ₹1; the client invalidates the investments and transactions caches.

The Link… dialog disables the kind with a reason on a DEBIT ("Dividends must be money-in (credit) transactions"), on a multi-selection, and on a transaction that already carries a ledger, loan or dividend ref (client-side rule in useTransactionLink ; the server itself allows several dividend rows on one credit). Linking clears any manual receipt note.

Alternative: untracked account. If the payout went to a bank account FinanceOS does not track, edit the dividend → Receipt note → "Received in an untracked account" or "Not received (chasing)" (setting a note is refused with 400 while a credit is linked; clearing it is allowed) → PUT /{id}/receipt-status stores receipt_status . Server touches: dividends (transaction_id, receipt_status, tds), reads of transactions and the loan, lending and transaction_links tables for exclusion; events DIVIDEND_MATCH_ATTEMPTED , DIVIDEND_LINKED . Failure points: a credit already used by a loan, lending or another family is silently absent from candidates (and refused with 400 if sent directly); dividend amounts after a stock split may be too small to match (the split-ratio fuzzy tier needs a narration clue); a dividend with no bank coverage never turns Overdue. Section 22
Executive summary

The codebase is consistent and disciplined in its patterns (layered server, typed client boundary, idempotent migrations, tenancy aspect, exhaustive E2E). Its weaknesses are the ones typical of fast AI-assisted growth: a handful of very large classes, duplicated logic (three sign conventions, two KPI engines, two FY definitions), dead code left after redesigns, stale documentation, and no optimistic locking. Quality is high where a plan document exists and lower where a fix was made in place. Confirmed for all measurements; ratings are the author's judgement.

Consistent module layout : controller → service → repository → entity per domain; DTOs as records; validation via Jakarta annotations.
Explicit invariants in plans : rewards, loans, lendings, corporate actions have plan documents that match the code's shape.
Observability : request ids end to end, JSON logs with MDC, Faro in the client, structured job results.

Section 23
Executive summary

Tenant isolation is the strongest part of the system: three independent mechanisms, exhaustively swept by E2E. Secrets at rest are encrypted with AES-GCM under two master keys. The material findings are one missing OAuth state check (login CSRF), unencrypted statement PDFs kept as job artifacts for up to 7 days, a session cap that never frees slots, a committed session-cookie file, and a set of operational exposures on the single VM. Confirmed

Sections 24 and 58
Executive summary

FinanceOS is a compute-on-read system running on a 512 MB heap with two job threads. Every derived number (balance, positions, rewards, schedules) is recomputed per request from full history. This is correct and cheap at personal scale (thousands of transactions) and will degrade linearly with history; nothing is cached server-side. The client side is well tuned (RSC prefetch, 30 s staleTime, server pagination, code-split charts). Confirmed for mechanisms; no load measurements exist in the repository.

Every arrow is recomputed on each request. The two multiplicative nodes (Card Picker × cards, portfolio_value × month ends) are where cost grows fastest. The bug the integration tests found: section isolation

The first implementation of Upcoming ( ObligationsService ) and the net_worth datasource wrapped each section in a try/catch so that one broken section (a malformed loan schedule, a failing bill query) would only drop that section's rows. Mockito unit tests passed. The Spring integration tests ( ObligationsSectionIsolationIntegrationTest , NetWorthSectionIsolationIntegrationTest ) made a @SpyBean collaborator throw and showed the whole read returning 500: the failing collaborator was a @Transactional bean that had joined the caller's read-only transaction, so its interceptor marked that shared transaction rollback-only before the exception reached the catch, and the commit then threw UnexpectedRollbackException . Fix (server 9be54db): every section runs through SectionRunner ; the Spring implementation TransactionalSectionRunner opens a REQUIRES_NEW read-only transaction per section, so a failure rolls back only that section. Unit tests use SectionRunner.DIRECT . Confirmed

Executive summary

The 95 migrations and the plans directory tell the system's history. It began as a bank-transaction tracker (V1–V25) and grew Gmail ingestion, statements and the review workflow (V26–V40). Investments, F&O and loans followed (V41–V50), then a full rewards engine (V51–V61), then LLM plumbing, chat and account lifecycle (V62–V85). The latest band adds lending links, notification markers and the navigation redesign (V86–V95). Four areas were redesigned rather than extended: the credit-card model (three times), lendings (repayments → ledger), the client data path (server-first → TanStack), and navigation (feature menus → Home, Inbox and Upcoming, with built-in widgets). Confirmed from migration files; dates from memory notes where present.

ADR-16 Built-in dashboard widgets come from a code registry ( BuiltinWidgetRegistry ), not from report rows seeded per user Home needs the same widgets for every user, some are not reports at all (Inbox, Bills due render their own component), and seeded rows would freeze each user's copy of the definition Widget JSON stores only kind: builtin , builtinKey , params . Templates run through ReportDataService.runDefinition on every read, so a server release changes every user's widget at once. Built-ins can only be removed (not edited) and must keep minW . Users who want to change one use "Duplicate as my report". Only "Spend this month" is seeded as a real report so that the user can edit it. A key removed from the registry leaves stored widgets with no ref. Confirmed

ADR-17 The Inbox is computed on read from the producers' own rows; only the user's snooze and dismiss are stored ( inbox_item_state ), with no notifications table V90–V92 already chose markers on producer rows over a notification log. A stored inbox would need its own lifecycle in step with bills, EMIs, statements and jobs The Inbox is never stale and never needs a backfill. Listing is strictly read-only: it never calls a producer's evaluate and never advances a marker, so opening it cannot send a push. In exchange, each kind's "is this due" rule exists twice (collector and push producer), push links copy the collector window ( BillMessages.href , EmiMessages.href ), the summary endpoint costs a full list, and state rows for vanished items are never pruned. Confirmed

ADR-18 Composite reads (Upcoming obligations, net_worth ) run each section through SectionRunner , in its own REQUIRES_NEW read-only transaction A plain try/catch was not enough. When a @Transactional collaborator throws inside the shared transaction, its interceptor marks that transaction rollback-only, and the caller's commit then fails with UnexpectedRollbackException (HTTP 500). The integration tests in 9be54db found this. One failing section drops only its own rows and logs an event. Each section takes its own pooled connection while the outer transaction is suspended. The tenant filter is re-enabled by the collaborators' own @Transactional boundaries. SectionRunner.DIRECT runs sections inline in plain unit tests, so only the Spring/H2 integration tests prove the isolation. The Inbox does not use it. Confirmed
Domain boundaries (§62)

Well-separated : Wealth (its own brokers table, no coupling to bank transactions except the broker's balance), Debt (loans link to transactions only through payments), Core. Leaky : Insight reads every domain's tables directly through SQL (reports) and views (chat), so any schema change ripples into DatasourceCatalog , the executors and the v_chat_* views. Shared kernel : transactions is touched by Gmail, files, statements, categorization, rewards, loans and merge; it is the coupling point of the system.

Attention (navigation redesign, server 9e02b6c) is a read-side layer over the other domains and owns almost no data. domain/obligations ( ObligationsService ) merges loan schedules, lending dues, card bills ( CardBillService in domain/notification/bill ) and expected statements. domain/inbox owns inbox_item_state and the collectors. The collectors reuse the push producers' static rules ( BillNotificationService.isStale , EmiNotificationService.currentInstallment , LendingReturnNotificationService.dueObligations , StatementExpectedNotificationService.overduePeriodEnd , JobNotificationService.NOTIFIED_TYPES ) but never call evaluate . domain/dashboard owns BuiltinWidgetRegistry and HomeDashboardSeeder . The net_worth , obligations and attention datasources plug the layer into reports, so Insight now depends on it. The boundary leaks in two places. Inbox collectors depend on notification internals, so changing a producer's rule changes the Inbox. BillMessages and EmiMessages import InboxKinds to build push links, so the dependency also runs back from notifications to the Inbox. Confirmed from imports.

Gotchas for newcomers
Mockito tests never boot Spring or Flyway. Always boot the server after schema or config changes.
Client tests need Node 20; the default Node 18 crashes vitest.
Amounts are positive in the DB with a type ; the API re-signs them. Do not add signs in SQL without checking the three existing CASE expressions.
Each sub-repository has its own git; use git -C when diffing.
A new entity is not tenant-safe until it has @Filter(name="userFilter") .
Migrations must be idempotent PL/SQL and must not use parallel DML on ADB.
Regenerate schema.d.ts after any DTO change or CI fails on drift.
Radix asChild triggers drop streamed RSC children; use children plus triggerClassName .
The READMEs describe an older architecture; trust this handbook and the code.

Catching an exception inside a @Transactional read does not contain it when the failing bean is itself transactional: the shared transaction is already rollback-only. Use SectionRunner for independent sections of a composite read.
The Inbox must stay read-only: collectors read producers' rows and markers and never call evaluate , or opening the Inbox would push and advance markers.
GET /dashboards writes on a user's first call (Home seeding). Tests and E2E specs that count dashboards see Home; a new user never starts with zero dashboards.
The "is it in the Inbox" rule lives twice, in the collectors and in the push link builders ( BillMessages.href , EmiMessages.href ); change both.
Moved pages keep redirect stubs: /settings/ingest → /transactions/import , /settings/jobs → /settings/activity (query kept), /loans/calendar → /upcoming . Link to the new paths.
Integration tests share one H2 database across @SpringBootTest classes; delete every row a test creates.

If I only read ten things

The ledger is transactions , everything else is derived. Balances, rewards, positions, schedules and reports are recomputed on every read from source rows. There are no cached totals to go stale, and no cached totals to protect you from a wrong formula. §10
Trust is a state, not a boolean. Every ingested row carries a review status and reasons; the statement is the reconciliation truth that promotes alerts. Manual rows are trusted by definition. §38
Tenancy is enforced three ways (Hibernate filter, explicit binds, Oracle-side context for chat) and swept by E2E for every endpoint. It is the most trustworthy part of the system. §15
The credit-card model is on its third design (account → cardholder → card). Reward scoping, Gmail resolution and statements all hang off it; touch it carefully. M1

Rewards are a rules engine with an exclusive chain and shared caps , evaluated per transaction with a reason code. Duplicate rules double-pay; point value defaults disagree between the report and the Card Picker. M7
Reports over-count multi-category transactions because of a join fan-out; chat does not. When two numbers disagree, this is the first suspect. §45 C1
Google OAuth never checks state . This is the one security finding to fix before anything else. §23
XIRR has no tests and uses doubles. Every return figure rests on it. §25

Everything asynchronous is a job in the DB run by two threads in the API JVM; failures surface in job results, the Gmail attention queue and the Inbox (finished jobs from the last week), not in alerts. §14
The plans directory is intent, the code is truth, and they disagree in known places (charges in cost basis, EMI match tolerance, is_excluded). The READMEs are stale. §45 §31
The mental model

Picture a single append-mostly ledger of money movements per person, fed by three intakes of decreasing trust: hand entry, bank statements, and LLM-read emails. Around the ledger sit five calculators that never store their answers: a balance calculator anchored to statements, a reward calculator that replays card rules, a portfolio calculator that replays trades and corporate actions in FIFO order, a loan calculator that regenerates amortization schedules, and a report engine that aggregates whatever it is pointed at. A job queue in the same process does the slow intake work on a timer. A model can be asked questions and answers by writing SQL against read-only views that already carry the tenant boundary. Three front doors sit on top of all this, and they are computed too: Home (a seeded dashboard of widgets), the Inbox (what needs attention now) and Upcoming (what falls due). The whole thing runs on free tiers, so quotas, cooldowns and small heaps shape many of its behaviours. If a number looks wrong, the question is never "which cache is stale" but always "which source row is wrong, or which formula".

Final master summary

FinanceOS is a single-person-scale personal finance system for an Indian household: a Spring Boot API over Oracle with a Next.js client, that ingests money movements from Gmail alerts and statements, lets the owner review and categorize them, and derives balances, credit-card rewards, investment positions, loan schedules, reports and chat answers on demand. It is well isolated per tenant, well tested at the wiring level, and deployed through a strict pipeline to a single small VM. Its financial numbers are trustworthy for balances, card dues, F&O and lendings; need a second look for rewards, positions and loans versus outside sources; and are known-wrong for category-grouped report totals with multi-category rows and unverified for XIRR. The three actions with the best return are validating OAuth state, fixing the category join, and writing XIRR goldens. Beyond that, the codebase would benefit most from deleting its dead code, reconciling its duplicated logic, and committing the large body of reviewed but unshipped work.
